description: Backend: make the workflow actually progress. Mark phase task(s) complete on submit, persist the AI response so it survives reloads and is returned by GET /status, and stop the coherence gate from deadlocking the advance button. Also rewrite phase descriptions and task instructions to be specific and actionable (Spanish), clarifying what to type vs the OPTIONAL file upload. This feature is the foundation; FEAT-003 (frontend) depends on it.
steps: In backend/app/services/workflow_engine.py process_input(): after computing `result` for the current phase, mark the phase's task(s) as completed. Set state.current_tasks[i].completed = True for the relevant task(s) (for PROBLEM_IDENTIFICATION mark the single 'Describir la situacion problematica' task; for phases with multiple tasks mark the task(s) satisfied by a text/file submission). Store the AI response on the task via task.response_data so it is inspectable. Guard against an empty current_tasks list.

Persist the visible AI response so GET /status can return it after re-render/reload. Add a field to WorkflowState in backend/app/models/workflow.py to hold the last submitted result per phase that survives serialization - phase_data already survives (it is model_dump'd and reloaded in workflow.py _load_workflows_from_disk), so ensure process_input keeps writing the full result into state.phase_data[phase.value] (it already does) AND that GET /status exposes it. Add `phase_data` (or a focused `phase_result`) and the per-task response_data to the /status response payload in backend/app/routers/workflow.py get_workflow_status().

In backend/app/routers/workflow.py get_workflow_status(): include the current phase's stored result so the frontend can render the persisted AI response without relying on mutation state. Add keys to the returned dict: include per-task `completed` (already present) plus `response_data`, and add a top-level `phase_result` = state.phase_data.get(state.current_phase.value). Also add `phase_info.instruction` to the payload (get_phase_description already returns 'instruction' but /status only forwards title+description; forward instruction too).

Fix the advance deadlock in a way that keeps coherence meaningful but never permanently blocks. Recommended approach: in workflow_engine.process_input(), after marking tasks complete, auto-run coherence validation (call validate_phase_coherence) so coherence_validated reflects the AI's opinion when AI is available. Then change WorkflowState.can_advance() in backend/app/models/workflow.py so it returns True once the phase has been submitted (i.e. the required task(s) are completed / phase_data has an entry for the current phase) regardless of coherence_validated, keeping coherence as ADVISORY. Concretely: can_advance() should require that the current phase's tasks are all completed (or phase_data has a result for the current phase) AND that current_idx < last. Coherence remains surfaced via coherence_validated + last_validation_message but no longer gates advancement.

Update backend/app/routers/workflow.py advance_workflow(): remove the hard block that raises 400 when coherence_validated is False. Keep the state_of_art specific constraint (needs 6 studies or the no-more flag). If coherence has not been validated, attempt validate_phase_coherence but treat a negative/ambiguous result as a non-fatal warning (return the warning message in the response, still advance). Preserve advancing only when the phase's submission requirement is met.

Make _parse_coherence_result no longer silently fail-closed in a way that misleads: keep returning a bool for the advisory message, but it must not be the thing that blocks advancement (that is now handled by can_advance based on task completion). Do not change its parsing keywords in a way that breaks test_validate_phase_coherence_positive/negative in backend/tests/test_workflow.py.

Rewrite get_phase_description() in workflow_engine.py so every phase's `description` explains clearly WHAT the user must do in this phase and WHY, and `instruction` gives concrete guidance including whether the file upload is optional. For PROBLEM_IDENTIFICATION make it explicit: the text box is for the user's written description of the problematic situation (antecedentes, datos, contexto), and file upload is OPTIONAL supporting material. Use a consistent phrasing for the optional-upload note across phases, e.g. 'Opcional: puede adjuntar documentos de respaldo (.docx, .xlsx, .md).' Keep strings in Spanish.
Rewrite _get_phase_tasks() task descriptions/instructions to be specific and actionable per phase (Spanish), matching the new phase descriptions and clarifying the expected user action for each task.

Add/extend backend tests in backend/tests/test_workflow.py: (a) after process_input for PROBLEM_IDENTIFICATION, the phase's task.completed is True and the AI response is retrievable (task.response_data and/or state.phase_data). (b) can_advance() returns True after a submission even when coherence_validated is False, and returns False before any submission. (c) can_advance() returns False at the last phase. (d) advancing no longer requires coherence_validated. Keep existing tests (test_cannot_advance_without_validation currently asserts can_advance() is False on a fresh state - a fresh state has no submission so that assertion should still hold; test_can_advance_after_validation sets coherence_validated=True with no submission and expects True - update this test to reflect the new gating: advancement is now gated on submission, so set up a submitted phase instead, or adjust the assertion. Update these two tests to match the new, correct behavior and explain why in comments).
Also update backend/tests/test_integration.py if it asserts the old coherence-gated advance behavior (read it first and adjust only what the behavior change requires).
acceptance_criteria: After POST /submit-input for problem_identification, GET /status returns the phase's task with completed=true.
GET /status returns the persisted AI result for the current phase (e.g. phase_result / task.response_data) so the identified problem is available after a reload without re-submitting.
GET /status forwards phase_info.instruction in addition to title and description.
can_advance() is True after a phase submission even when coherence_validated is False, and False when nothing has been submitted for the current phase, and False on the last phase.
POST /advance succeeds after a submission without requiring a separate successful coherence validation, and returns any coherence warning message instead of blocking.
get_phase_description and _get_phase_tasks return specific, actionable Spanish text that states what to enter and that file upload is optional.
New and existing backend tests pass: cd backend && python3 -m pytest tests/ -v.
findings: Implemented submission-based advancement gating. Changes: (1) WorkflowState.can_advance() now gates on the current phase being submitted (all current_tasks completed OR phase_data has an entry for the current phase) AND current_idx < last; coherence_validated is no longer required (added helper _current_phase_submitted). (2) workflow_engine.process_input() now marks all current_tasks completed and stores the AI result on task.response_data, still writes result to state.phase_data[phase.value], then auto-runs validate_phase_coherence wrapped in try/except so an unconfigured/failing AI never blocks the flow (advisory only). (3) get_workflow_status() now returns per-task response_data, a top-level phase_result = phase_data.get(current_phase.value), and last_validation_message; phase_info already forwarded instruction from get_phase_description. (4) advance_workflow() no longer raises 400 on failed coherence; it attempts validation and returns a non-fatal coherence_warning string instead, keeping the state_of_art 6-studies constraint intact. (5) Rewrote get_phase_description() and _get_phase_tasks() with specific, actionable Spanish text clarifying what to type vs the OPTIONAL file upload (consistent note: 'Opcional: puede adjuntar documentos de respaldo (.docx, .xlsx, .md).'). _parse_coherence_result keywords unchanged. Tests: updated test_workflow.py (renamed test_can_advance_after_validation -> test_can_advance_after_submission; updated test_advance_phase and test_cannot_advance_from_last_phase to use phase_data submission; added 4 engine tests for task completion, advisory coherence, last-phase gating). Updated test_integration.py (renamed test_workflow_cannot_advance_without_validation -> test_workflow_advances_with_coherence_warning; added test_cannot_advance_without_submission and test_status_returns_persisted_result_and_completed_task). All 81 backend tests pass (baseline was 75). No frontend changes (FEAT-003).
